title: Full-Stack Architecture & Orientation
outcome: Explain the complete TaskFlow request path and identify which layer owns presentation, transport, business rules, persistence, identity, and operations.
artifact: A one-page architecture map plus an ADR-style note describing the responsibilities of Next.js, NestJS, Prisma, PostgreSQL/Supabase, and supporting infrastructure.
labSteps: Draw TaskFlow as boxes and arrows before opening an IDE.
Label every arrow with what crosses it: props, HTTP JSON, verified identity, Prisma calls, SQL results.
Write one responsibility and one non-responsibility for each layer.
Trace create-task from click to database commit and back to the screen.
Trace one failure: invalid input, missing authentication, forbidden action, database outage.
Record the architecture decisions that should remain stable through later phases.
failureModes: Putting business rules in React components
Letting controllers call the database directly everywhere
Treating Supabase as one undifferentiated magic backend
mastery: Can trace a request without skipping a layer
Can explain why the API owns rules
Can name which concerns are deployment concerns rather than business logic
principles: Map every request from browser to frontend, API, database, and back before adding abstractions.
Keep presentation, business rules, and persistence responsibilities intentionally separated.
Treat TaskFlow as one continuous system so each phase extends an architecture you already understand.
Use version locks as a reproducibility contract, not as a reason to ignore underlying concepts.

quiz.question: Which practice best matches Phase 00's engineering goal?
options: Map every request from browser to frontend, API, database, and back before adding abstractions.
Move every concern into the frontend so the API stays thin.
Duplicate the same state in several places and synchronize it with effects.
Trust client-provided identity because the browser already logged in.
quiz.explanation: Map every request from browser to frontend, API, database, and back before adding abstractions.
